description: Square four-post canopy module roofed in overlapping nipa palm thatch, low gabled, open on all sides -- one bay of a covered market row.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Square four-post canopy module with a low gabled roof of overlapping nipa palm thatch panels, slender round timber posts at the four corners carrying a simple beam frame, open on all sides Materials: Sun-bleached grey-brown nipa palm leaf thatch laid in overlapping courses, fronds fraying and splitting at the eaves, darker damp underside, weathered hardwood posts with rope lashings at the joints.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92. 3,120/4,000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 3/6 unique geometries, two 512 px canvases. Open on all four sides: turntable with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope measured 4.000 x 3.200 x 4.000 m off the built module, nothing crossing the cell edge on either axis; four 150 mm posts at +-1.550 under a roof that owns +-2.000, so the eave and the verge overhang the post line by 0.45 m the way the plate and the proxy (0.121 H) show; plates 1.98-2.12, tie beams 2.12-2.24, eave 2.20, thatch apex 3.13, ridge plank top 3.200; a 24.9 degree gable with the ridge along X; open on all four sides. Post grid / roof span 0.775 against the proxy's 0.757.
featureReviews.notes: One deliberate divergence from the plate and proxy, recorded: the pitch is 24.9 degrees against the proxy's 39, because the ridge is declared at 3.20 and the eave cannot drop below what keeps 1.98 m of headroom under the head frame. The first build had 18.3 degrees and posts on the cell edge with no overhang, which was the largest single fidelity loss.

featureReviews.evidence: One 48 x 12 height grid carrying both slopes; six courses per 1.60 m tile with a per-column jittered butt, torn blade tips past every butt, blade seams, a lit-tip line over a 0.70 shadow gradient, gaps and two rot patches; a torn fringe as a per-column 0-0.42 m drop in the eave rows AND a per-row 0-0.32 m drop in the verge columns -- real silhouette, no modelled fronds. Up-facing slope re-authored after measuring 162 against the plate's 150 in a matched window; the underside seen through the gables is a darker vertex tone.
featureReviews.notes: At hero distance the fringe reads as a fringe of blades; the plate's are finer than an 83 mm column can carry, and the next step in grid density costs the triangle budget.

featureReviews.evidence: Stacked plates and tie beams with their ends running past the posts, eight short knee braces, a rope wrap at every plate-tie crossing and two cord collars down each post head; two king posts, a ridge beam, four pairs of rafters (the outer pair at the verge) and eight instanced purlins whose ends show under the verges, all visible through the open gable ends at azimuth 90 and 270. Timber authored as the inverse of the two-point harness probe, posts pulled to a neutral grey.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's timber is greyer and more contrasted than the render's; the tile is a multiplier and a stronger grain would push shaded faces toward the backdrop band.

name: Nipa Thatch Canopy Module
nameTh: หลังคาจากใบจาก
notes: One bay of a modular outdoor roof kit: 4 x 4 m footprint on a 4 m grid, which divides the kit's 8 m ground and road tiles exactly 2 x 2, so a canopy grid lands on the paving grid. Four corner posts, because the brief is a module that includes its own poles and must therefore stand alone; the posts are INSET 0.45 m from the cell edge (centres at +-1.55) so the roof overhangs them the way a real nipa shelter does, and bays placed side by side stand their posts 0.90 m apart under one continuous roof. Gabled with the ridge across the module, so bays butted along the ridge axis continue one roof and bays butted across it read as a row of repeated gables. Ridge at 3.2 m. Eave: the original 2.4 m was a clearance figure, and clearance is under the HEAD FRAME at the post line, not at the eave edge 0.45 m outside the posts -- so the eave top is 2.20 m (24.9 degree pitch, 0.93 rise over 2.00 m) and the frame is stacked to keep 1.98 m of headroom: posts to 1.98, plates 1.98-2.12, tie beams 2.12-2.24, thatch underside at the post line 2.23. The torn fringe hangs to about 1.6 m at the cell edge, where a player meets it only from the open side. Open on all sides -- no walls, no infill, no hanging goods. Thatch depth is carried by the texture and the fringe silhouette, not by modelled fronds, which would spend the whole triangle budget on the one thing a normal map does well.
